author: WP16
summary: Alpha.1-era chapter on sharp-runtime's include roots and transliteration rule, namespace-to-component mapping, CNA's direct header subset, String/StringBuilder, Stream and MemoryStream semantics, UTF8Encoding validation and generic task limits. Counts (1,032 headers, 54 CNA includes) and the local UTF-8 validator are stale at 41b918c9 (1,097; 81; shared TryDecodeUtf8Scalar), and ObjectModel/Collection.hpp belongs to Collections.Core. The site had none of the stream, encoding or task semantics; they now live on the components and streams/text/tasks deep dives.

concepts.section: Namespaces, Types, and Include Paths
concepts.text: sharp-runtime makes a source-porting promise visible: knowing a .NET fully qualified name predicts the include, while the component registry answers which component owns it and what follows transitively.

concepts.section: Two public roots, no umbrella
concepts.text: Public headers at 41b918c9: 1,097 below two roots (1,090 System/, 7 SharpRuntime/), plus 9 private headers under module src/ trees.

concepts.section: Two public roots, no umbrella
concepts.text: Private headers under a module's src/ are not on consumer include paths because a component's include directory is its module include/ only.

concepts.section: Two public roots, no umbrella
concepts.text: One public type per like-named header is the norm, so an include not derivable from the type name deserves inspection and a private include cannot hide behind an umbrella.

concepts.section: Namespaces do not equal components one-for-one
concepts.text: C++ namespaces describe API identity and CMake components describe build ownership; families split across components (ObjectModel's Collection lives in Collections.Core, ObservableCollection in Collections.ObjectModel).
tokens: the namespace alone does not name the component

concepts.section: Namespaces do not equal components one-for-one
concepts.text: Representative mapping: TimeSpan -> Core.Base, List -> Collections.Core, MemoryStream -> IO, UTF8Encoding -> Text, Task -> Threading.Tasks, SHA256 -> Security.Cryptography, ResourceManager -> Resources.

concepts.section: Namespaces do not equal components one-for-one
concepts.text: The direct component is not the full closure; CNA names SharpRuntime::IO instead of copying IO's current dependency list.

concepts.section: CNA's dependency subset
concepts.text: Counting only the SharpRuntime/ prefix and concluding CNA uses two runtime headers mistakes a namespace prefix for a repository boundary; CNA includes 81 distinct headers at TARGET.
tokens: mistakes a namespace prefix for a repository boundary

concepts.section: CNA's dependency subset
concepts.text: SharpRuntimeHelper.hpp is unusually load-bearing: 389 public sharp-runtime headers include it and CNA uses its aliases throughout.

concepts.section: CNA's dependency subset
concepts.text: SharpRuntimeHelper.hpp exports two unnamespaced macros, CONTAINS and INTERNAL, which consumers must treat as global preprocessor names.

concepts.section: CNA's dependency subset
concepts.text: Prop.hpp is an exported downstream facility: sharp-runtime's own properties are hand-written, while CNA's Viewport.hpp, ContentManager.hpp and sensor headers declare properties with DEF_PROP.
concepts.note: Only the Experimental property headers include it inside sharp-runtime.

concepts.section: CNA's dependency subset
concepts.text: Prop.hpp defines 31 macro names including ordinary words (YES, NO, nothing), so every translation unit including Viewport.hpp or ContentManager.hpp inherits them.

concepts.section: String and StringBuilder: static utility versus mutable buffer
concepts.text: System::String is a pure static utility over std::string (IsNullOrEmpty, Compare, IndexOf/LastIndexOf, Split, Substring, Trim*, PadLeft/PadRight).

concepts.section: String and StringBuilder: static utility versus mutable buffer
concepts.text: StringBuilder offers overloaded Append (including longcs), AppendLine, Insert, Remove, Replace and a ChunkEnumerator that always yields one chunk.

concepts.section: String and StringBuilder: static utility versus mutable buffer
concepts.text: StringBuilder lengths and indices are UTF-8 bytes, so Remove(1, 1) on u8"\u00e9A" leaves the ill-formed pair c3 41 (declared deviation #2015).

concepts.section: Stream: a lightweight subset, honest about it
concepts.text: IO::Stream is a lightweight subset: Read, Close and getLengthProperty are pure virtual; Write/WriteByte and Position default to NotSupportedException.
tokens: lightweight subset of the .NET Stream API

concepts.section: Stream: a lightweight subset, honest about it
concepts.text: CanWrite defaults to false and CanRead to true, a read-only stream's honest self-report; a writable or unreadable subclass must override them.
tokens: every capability you implement, you also report

concepts.section: MemoryStream: writable by default, read-only when requested
concepts.text: CNA's ContentManager::OpenStream and ResourceContentManager read each asset fully and return a read-only MemoryStream(bytes, size, false); assets above INT32_MAX bytes raise ContentLoadException.
concepts.note: Bible limited the use to Android APK assets.

concepts.section: MemoryStream: writable by default, read-only when requested
concepts.text: The default MemoryStream is empty and writable; the copy constructor MemoryStream(const bytecs*, intcs, bool writable = true) makes the default explicit and allows a read-only copy.

concepts.section: MemoryStream: writable by default, read-only when requested
concepts.text: Constructor validation: null with non-zero size -> ArgumentNullException (checked first), negative size -> ArgumentOutOfRangeException, and (nullptr, 0) accepted as an empty range.

concepts.section: MemoryStream: writable by default, read-only when requested
concepts.text: Passing writable=false gives a readable, seekable, non-writable copy whose Write and WriteByte throw NotSupportedException.

concepts.section: Closing a memory stream closes operations, not the bytes it already owns
concepts.text: MemoryStream::Close() only clears the open flag; Read/Write/Seek/Length/Position then throw ObjectDisposedException and CanRead/CanSeek become false.

concepts.section: Closing a memory stream closes operations, not the bytes it already owns
concepts.text: A closed stream created writable keeps CanWrite true, as .NET's property reports the construction-time flag.

concepts.section: Closing a memory stream closes operations, not the bytes it already owns
concepts.text: ToArray() and GetBuffer() stay usable after Close, following .NET's Dispose which keeps the buffer; ensureNotClosed() guards only operations.

concepts.section: Closing a memory stream closes operations, not the bytes it already owns
concepts.text: ToArray() returns an independent vector, while GetBuffer() returns a reference to the live vector that a reallocation can invalidate.

concepts.section: Closing a memory stream closes operations, not the bytes it already owns
concepts.text: Null buffers and negative offsets or counts throw instead of returning an end-of-stream zero.

concepts.section: Closing a memory stream closes operations, not the bytes it already owns
concepts.text: Writes past a Position beyond the end compute position+count in int64_t and throw IOException('Stream was too long.') instead of overflowing; StreamTests sets Position 2147483647 to require it.

concepts.section: UTF8Encoding: conformance validation and fallback evidence
concepts.text: UTF8Encoding's GetBytes/GetString validate well-formed UTF-8 and route each ill-formed byte through the fallback rather than passing bytes through.
tokens: validate that the input is well-formed UTF-8

concepts.section: UTF8Encoding: conformance validation and fallback evidence
concepts.text: Validation now lives in one shared function, System::detail::TryDecodeUtf8Scalar (tickets #2014, #2354); wellFormedUtf8Length() is a thin wrapper.
concepts.note: Bible described a local grammar walk in UTF8Encoding.cpp.

concepts.section: UTF8Encoding: conformance validation and fallback evidence
concepts.text: Overlong encodings, surrogates U+D800-U+DFFF, values above U+10FFFF and bad continuation bytes are rejected; overlong C0 AF is the historical filter-bypass shape.

concepts.section: UTF8Encoding: conformance validation and fallback evidence
concepts.text: The constructor installs U+FFFD replacement fallbacks as .NET's UTF8Encoding.SetDefaultFallbacks() does, not the base Encoding's '?'.

concepts.section: UTF8Encoding: conformance validation and fallback evidence
concepts.text: Replacement is one U+FFFD per invalid byte: a two-byte overlong sequence becomes two replacement characters, a lone continuation byte one.

concepts.section: UTF8Encoding: conformance validation and fallback evidence
concepts.text: Regression evidence: UTF8EncodingTests, Utf8SharedScalarDecodeTests and the Utf8Tests span-validator family (named, not executed).

concepts.section: Generic continuations exist; generic combinators do not
concepts.text: Task and TaskT<TResult> both implement ContinueWith with inline callbacks; TaskT has an action overload returning Task and a result overload returning TaskT<TNewResult>.

concepts.section: Generic continuations exist; generic combinators do not
concepts.text: Both task implementations capture the antecedent state weakly to avoid a cycle from its continuation list back to itself.

concepts.section: Generic continuations exist; generic combinators do not
concepts.text: WhenAll and WhenAny accept only std::vector<Task>; there is no generic overload producing a result array or typed winner.

concepts.section: Generic continuations exist; generic combinators do not
concepts.text: The lightweight antecedent handed to a callback shares status, result and exception but not the cancellation token, which reads CancellationToken::None().

concepts.section: Reading a dependency from source
concepts.text: A dependency review derives the include from the FQN, finds the module owning that include/ file, then reads the component's declared public dependencies.

concepts.section: Reading a dependency from source
concepts.text: Namespace, directory and link depth usually agree, but umbrellas and the Xml.XPath alias are exceptions where the registry is authoritative.

concepts.section: Reading a dependency from source
concepts.text: Include availability is weaker than semantic parity: a resolving header proves a type can be named, not that every .NET behaviour behind it exists.
tokens: a header that resolves proves only that a type can be named

issues.text: Public CNA headers (Viewport.hpp, ContentManager.hpp, sensor readings) include SharpRuntime/Prop.hpp, which defines 31 unnamespaced macros including YES, NO and nothing; SharpRuntimeHelper.hpp adds CONTAINS and INTERNAL.
